entry.label: Positive feedback
entry.description: A feedback relation in which returned effects reinforce the direction of change. It can amplify, switch, latch, tip or oscillate depending on loop gain, delay, saturation and constraints.
entry.canonical_definition: A feedback relation in which the returned effect reinforces rather than counteracts a change in the relevant variable; the sign, loop gain, delay and limiting conditions must be specified.

profile.title: Positive feedback
profile.canonical_definition: A feedback relation in which the returned effect reinforces rather than counteracts a change in the relevant variable; the sign, loop gain, delay and limiting conditions must be specified.
profile.summary: Positive feedback reinforces change. It can create growth, escalation, tipping, latching, path dependence or oscillation. What stops the process is usually found in constraints, saturation, resource limits or another balancing loop.
profile.why_it_matters: Reinforcing loops explain why small differences can become large and why systems can move rapidly away from an apparently stable condition. They are central to contagion, polarisation, bubbles, collapse, learning and mobilisation, but are not inherently beneficial or harmful.
key_distinctions: reinforcing loop vs exponential growth without limit
historical_lineage: early regenerative circuits predate the cybernetic synthesis
mid-century control and cybernetics established positive and negative loop language
system dynamics popularised reinforcing loop notation
logical_antecedents: returned effect aligned with the direction of change
dependent_subsequents: escalation and vicious or virtuous circles
practice_connections: look for the limit that eventually stops growth
do not label the loop virtuous or vicious before examining consequences
test whether intervention also strengthens the loop
profile.editorial_note: Readable orientation and evidence-backed first pass. Not accepted scholarly consensus until named review is recorded.
